intended_object: The coordinate ring K[U_n] ⊗_K K[U_n^{(r)}] of the fibre product over Spec K of the unitriangular group scheme U_n and its closed r-th superdiagonal stage. Inferred from the docstring ("algebra of functions on the affine product of the ambient group and a stage") and from its use in `stageProductIso` via `pullbackSpecIso`.
explanation: The body is exactly Mathlib's `TensorProduct K (ambientRing K n) (stageRing K n r)`. The `@` form only names the instances explicitly (the commutative semiring structure on K, the additive monoid structures of the two rings, and their K-module structures from the algebra structures); it does not change the meaning. The next declaration, `stageProductIso`, uses `pullbackSpecIso` to identify the product of the two group schemes in `Over (Spec K)` with Spec of this ring, which confirms it is the coordinate ring of the affine product, as the docstring says. K is an arbitrary commutative ring, which is the natural generality. The object is a specific ring built from two particular group schemes, so being specific does not make it too narrow. Mathlib has no separate declaration for this ring; the general construction it uses is `TensorProduct` itself. It is essentially a helper abbreviation, but it denotes a genuine mathematical object and does so correctly.
